You write the prose of a GitHub pull request opened by Offramp. Offramp measured which LLM call sites of a repository NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory can take over, patched the ones that passed, and renders every number of the PR itself from the measurements.

Return JSON: {"summary": str, "sites": [{"site_id": str, "note": str}]}.
- summary: two or three plain sentences for the reviewer: what this PR changes and how the evidence was produced (agreement with references on a held-out split; the repo's own tests run on the patch).
- one note per site, one sentence, without repeating its decision label: for a migrated site, what changed in the call and why the function's behaviour is kept; for a kept site, why it stays and one concrete next step; for a manual-review site, what a reviewer must check.
- Never state a number, percentage, price, latency or count, in digits or in words ("one", "five", "a dozen", "twice"): such prose is discarded. Identifiers such as cs_02, file names or model ids are fine.
- Do not count sites: write "the refund planner stays on its model", not "one site stays".
- Parity is agreement with references (expected outputs built for the evaluation), never with the original model, whose outputs were not recorded: do not claim consistency or agreement with the original or prior model.
- Use only the facts given. No marketing language, no emoji.

message.content: {"summary": "This PR keeps all LLM call sites on their current models because none of the tested alternative tiers achieved sufficient parity with reference outputs on held-out cases. The decisions are based on evaluation results showing parity below the required threshold, and no migrations were applied.", "sites": [{"site_id": "cs_01", "note": "The triage ticket function remains on gpt-4o-mini as Lightning tier did not meet parity requirements despite adapter updates clarifying technical_support scope and adding few-shot examples."}, {"site_id": "cs_02", "note": "The next_action function stays on claude-sonnet-4-5 since no tested tier matched reference behavior closely enough, preserving the current tool-call selection logic."}, {"site_id": "cs_03", "note": "The extract_order function continues using claude-sonnet-4-5 as none of the tiers satisfied parity thresholds, maintaining the current email-to-order extraction rules."}, {"site_id": "cs_04", "note": "The answer_question function requires manual review due to a patch rejection where test setup text could not be located in the test file."}, {"site_id": "cs_05", "note": "The plan_refund function needs manual review after repo checks failed, specifically due to an assertion error about kwargs unpacking and a model mismatch in expectations."}, {"site_id": "cs_06", "note": "The summarize_thread function awaits manual review because the patch was rejected for failing to locate required adapter specification text in its test suite."}]}
